---
title: "D74 cutover runbooks"
description: "Order, commands, rollback pins and smoke for each app cutover to a Cloudflare Worker."
---

Cutovers run in this order: lowest risk first. Marketing page groups flip through the gateway instead (see the gateway Worker page). Each section is the whole runbook for one app; the linked packet has the full binding, secret and variable names.

## Web apex pin

Full rollback for the apex `tuturuuu.com` (Vercel project `platform`, apps/web): `dpl_FZuaw8J2RRS3ust79agjwyKo2AAf` (source d209d72b). The current production deployment is `dpl_9NxJS4nsCaYZwEjSWe2bJwj2Hjdk` (prebuilt from a7826c1f). Pins read 9 Nov 23:40.

## Common steps

1. Record the source SHA, the sealed artifact (CI run id) and the rollback evidence listed for the app.
2. Download the artifact: `gh run download <run-id> -R tutur3u/platform -n <artifact-name> -D /tmp/<app>-cutover`.
   Take the run id from a run on the production ref (`main`) at the accepted source SHA, and verify the run's head SHA. Never take an artifact by name alone: a name can match a pull-request run.
   Apps that upload a sealed archive (`<app>-cutover.tar.gz`: Chat, Hive, Playground, Rewise, Tools, Workspace) must be restored and verified with their own artifact tool in a checkout of the accepted SHA before step 4, exactly as the workflow's restore step does. For Rewise: `python3 scripts/ci/rewise-native-artifact.py restore apps/rewise --archive /tmp/rewise-cutover/rewise-cutover.tar.gz --receipt /tmp/rewise-cutover/restored.json`, then `verify apps/rewise --receipt /tmp/rewise-cutover/restored.json`. Step 4 then reads `apps/<app>/dist/server/wrangler.json` from that checkout instead of `/tmp/<app>-cutover/dist/server/wrangler.json`.
3. Secrets: set `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET` on every Worker to EXACTLY the value of Web's signer (the `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` value) and also set the same `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`. Drive, Mind and Rewise refuse requests when `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET` is unset, so leaving it unset is not an option. The dedicated signing value comes later through the accept-only slot (see the app-coordination secret rollout page).
4. Provision every secret name from the packet on the Worker BEFORE the code upload, then publish the artifact route-free with cf, never Wrangler. A Worker with the abuse guard (`ABUSE_GUARD` service binding) needs `ABUSE_GUARD_KEY_PEPPER` and the other required secrets set first; upload validation fails closed without them. Run from the repository root with `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` set to the Tuturuuu account and a scoped `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`. The converted output declares no routes or triggers, so nothing is routed yet.
   ```sh
   node scripts/ci/void-cf-output.mjs --config /tmp/<app>-cutover/dist/server/wrangler.json \
     --out /tmp/<app>-cf --name <worker> --sha <sha>
   # A Worker with no deployment yet: first publication. cf refuses required
   # secrets a Worker does not have yet, so pass them in a private 0600 JSON
   # file outside the repository and delete it afterwards.
   (cd /tmp/<app>-cf && "$OLDPWD/apps/calendar/node_modules/.bin/cf" deploy --prebuilt --mode production --no-provision \
     --secrets-file /tmp/<app>-secrets.json --message <sha>)
   # An existing Worker: upload a version, then move traffic while the captured version still serves.
   node scripts/ci/void-cf-publisher.mjs publish --build /tmp/<app>-cf --worker <worker> --message <sha> > /tmp/<app>-publish.json
   node scripts/ci/void-cf-publisher.mjs assign --worker <worker> \
     --version "$(jq -er .versionId /tmp/<app>-publish.json)" \
     --expect-current "$(jq -er .previousVersionId /tmp/<app>-publish.json)"
   ```
   See [cf CLI and Void over Wrangler](/build/development-tools/cf-cli-wrangler-parity#void-framework-app-publisher) for what the converter refuses.
5. Smoke the Worker on its own hostname before any route change: `node scripts/cutover-smoke.mjs <app> https://<worker-hostname>`. An artifact with `workers_dev` and `preview_urls` off has no such hostname; smoke it on the private acceptance host its packet names, or stop and ask the release authority for one, before step 6.
6. Attach the route or custom domain for the host (proxied, in front of the still-valid Vercel origin where possible). Proxied DNS flips happen only after the smoke in step 5 passes.
7. Re-run the smoke on the public host and watch for 5 minutes: no 5xx, login renders, entry route as expected.
8. Rollback on any 5xx above 1% for 5 minutes, a wrong redirect or a broken login. Calendar, Mail and Apps keep their active routes and use the [verified Cloudflare version rollback](/build/devops/wave1-cutover-packets#common). For the other packets that list a Vercel pin, remove the route or repoint the DNS record to that pin. No data or migration is involved.

### Pre-seal doctor

The artifact jobs of nova, rewise and the wave-1 apps run `scripts/ci/pre-seal-doctor.mjs` before the seal and pack. It starts the Worker from the emitted config in a disposable copy of `dist` (local workerd, synthetic secret values, every outbound request refused) and requests the PRODUCTION host with an explicit `Host` header. The seal is refused unless both answers hold:

- `GET /` answers 200, or with `--expect-redirect` a 30x whose `Location` is an auth path (`/login`, `/verify-token`). Pass the flag for apps that hand anonymous visitors to login; it is on for rewise, calendar and mail.
- `GET /api/build-info` answers 200 JSON whose `commitHash` equals the source SHA.

Any 401, 404 or 5xx on either request fails the step with the status and host in the message, so no seal exists for the app. It removes its temp directory and stops the Worker on every exit path and gives up after 120 seconds.

```sh
node scripts/ci/pre-seal-doctor.mjs <app> apps/<app> <production-host> <sha> [--expect-redirect] [--config dist/wave1/wrangler.json]
```

`--config` names the emitted Worker config inside the artifact directory (default `dist/server/wrangler.json`; the wave-1 production profile lives at `dist/wave1/wrangler.json`). It is the first check to run by hand against a downloaded artifact too.

Misses it exists to catch:

- nova: the production host is not in the Worker's `rootHosts`, so `/` and `/api/build-info` answer 404.
- rewise: the proxy rejects the anonymous build identity, so `/api/build-info` answers 401.
- apps: the production profile lacks `APPS_CANONICAL_HOST_ENABLED=1`, so every request answers 503 "Staging gateway only".

### Wave-1 apps (apps, calendar, mail)

Build these only as a production artifact. A plain `bun run build:cloudflare` produces the staging profile: the apps Worker then lacks `APPS_CANONICAL_HOST_ENABLED=1` and answers 503 "Staging gateway only", and calendar lacks `CALENDAR_DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE=production`. The production profile in `scripts/ci/wave1-native-profile.mjs` sets both.

1. `bun turbo:local run build --filter=@tuturuuu/<app> --concurrency=2` with `CALENDAR_DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE=production` (calendar) or `MAIL_DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE=production` (mail) exported.
2. `node scripts/ci/wave1-native-artifact.mjs prepare <app> production <sha>`.
3. `CI=true node scripts/ci/wave1-native-runtime.mjs <app> production <sha>`.
4. `node scripts/ci/wave1-native-artifact.mjs verify <app> production <sha>`.

Run it through `wave1-native-production.yaml` (input `app`, from the `production` ref) rather than by hand. The `build:cloudflare` steps in `apps-cloudflare.yaml` and `meet-cloudflare.yaml` build CI fixtures with placeholder Supabase values and are never a cutover artifact. Meet is not a wave-1 profile; its Worker is already live and is redeployed from `meet-cloudflare.yaml`.

### Mail deployment profile and staging Access

Every Mail build fixes one deployment profile at build time through `MAIL_DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE`: `production` or `staging` for a build, plus `development` for the dev server only. There is no default. A build or dev command without a valid value fails, so each workflow that builds Mail sets it explicitly (`turbo.json` hashes it, and `scripts/ci/mail-host-scan.test.mjs` fails when a Mail build path omits it).

| Profile | Root host | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| production | `mail.tuturuuu.com` | Serves the production host and mount hosts only; carries no Access names. |
| staging | the Access-protected staging host | Fronted by Cloudflare Access; the Worker also verifies the Access JWT itself. |

The staging Worker takes four extra secrets beyond the production set: `CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN` and `CF_ACCESS_AUD` verify the JWT (missing, foreign-key, wrong-AUD and expired tokens answer 403 before any route runs), and `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID` and `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET` form the service token attached only to server-side calls to the staging Web origin. Client Access credentials are stripped before any forward. Its R2 bucket is separate from the production bucket.

Each sealed artifact carries only its own environment's root host. `scripts/ci/mail-host-scan.mjs <dist> <profile>` runs on the original and the restored artifact and on the production qualification and CI builds: it rejects a production artifact that names the staging host, a staging artifact that names the production Supabase project, any folded `rootHosts` list other than the profile's own, and a staging request-forwarding source (`handler.ts`, `staging-access.ts`) that names a production host. The emitted-Worker acceptance in `wave1-native-runtime.mjs` serves fixture Access keys for staging, checks that missing, foreign-key, wrong-AUD, expired and malformed tokens are denied, and requires each artifact to answer 404 on the other environment's host.

- playground: no Vercel deployment found; staff-only app, routes attach at its own hostname when wanted.
